rationales.LC: Attacker-controlled invoice description free text is returned to the model inside a tool result and the model then calls approve_invoice, so language enters through ingested content and influences a privileged tool-invocation path.
rationales.CP: Each invoice starts a fresh message list, so there is no conversation memory; the invoice description is only re-retrieved source content and does not alter agent memory or standing behaviour.
rationales.AP: The effect is confined to the single FinBot agent and its own tool call; there are no handoffs, no other agents, and no trust-boundary crossing.
rationales.RH: The model can reach the approve_invoice write tool that sets status approved and payment_processed true, which is the reward/verifier channel on the path, but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented (prose walkthrough only, no payload or test).
rationales.ES: Five fixed tools are defined in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills, and the binding is fixed and allowlisted outside model output.

rh_facts.locus: approve_invoice tool that sets status approved and payment_processed true

score.automatable_rationale: The entry point is an unauthenticated HTTP API and the payload is a plain invoice description, so the attack can be scripted end to end without human interaction.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The write is confined to the invoice row (status approved, payment_processed true) and does not grant control of the host or the agent runtime.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the documented default an OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini model receives natural-language goals and chooses among five tools across up to five turns; the rule-based fallback applies only when no OpenAI client exists.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice processing assistant that pursues natural-language goals and selects approve, reject, or escalate tool calls.
